children: Trading volumes at the HDFC Bank counter may have fallen to a six-month low of about three crore shares in August, but fund managers have continued to accumulate the stock, buying shares worth around ₹13,530 crore during the month, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

August, which saw HDFC Bank shares decline 5.2%, witnessed significant buying by global and domestic fund managers. Vanguard Group acquired 12.92 crore shares, while Invesco and SBI Fund Managers bought 1.2 crore and 1.1 crore shares, respectively.

At the end of June 2026, Vanguard held around 2.4% stake in HDFC Bank through two of its funds — Vanguard Emerging Markets Stock Index Fund and Vanguard Total International Index Fund. The Malvern, Pennsylvania-headquartered asset manager now holds 4.52% in the bank, according to Bloomberg data.
Similarly, Invesco, which did not feature among HDFC Bank’s disclosed shareholders in June, now owns a 0.74% stake, while SBI Fund Managers held 5.5% as of August.

Cumulatively, 26 fund houses, including domestic and global investors, acquired nearly 19 crore shares of HDFC Bank during August, taking the value of their purchases to around ₹13,530 crore. The average closing price of the stock during the month stood at around ₹728.
On the other hand, Capital Group offloaded 1.4 crore shares of HDFC Bank in August, followed by JPMorgan Chase & Co, which sold another 81 lakh shares.

The combined monthly average trading volume of HDFC Bank across the BSE and NSE stood at 3.03 crore shares in August, with a turnover of ₹2,203 crore. This compares with 6.2 crore shares traded in March, with a turnover of ₹4,961 crore.

Meanwhile, HDFC Bank shares erased early gains after CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan’s surprise decision not to seek reappointment, shifting investor focus towards succession uncertainty at India’s largest private-sector lender by market capitalisation.
At least two brokerages, including Jefferies and Nuvama, lowered their target prices following the announcement, while HSBC downgraded the stock to “Hold” from “Buy”.
HDFC Bank shares have declined in seven of the last nine months, with the stock falling 5.2% in August, following a deeper 6.2% decline in July.

Macquarie, which retains an Outperform rating with a 12-month target price of ₹1,150, said the timing of Jagdishan’s departure adds another layer of uncertainty at a time when investor confidence is already fragile and the post-merger balance-sheet recalibration remains incomplete.

“Until the board provides greater clarity on its preferred candidate and transition framework, leadership uncertainty is likely to keep the stock in a narrow range,” said Suresh Ganapathy, MD and Head of India Research at Macquarie Capital.

Despite the recent weakness, analyst sentiment remains overwhelmingly positive. Of the 49 analysts tracking HDFC Bank, 47, or 96%, recommend a ‘Buy’, while the remaining two have a ‘Hold’ rating. There are currently no ‘Sell’ recommendations.
The 12-month average consensus price target stands at ₹1,001.09, implying an upside of around 41.2% from Monday’s NSE closing price of ₹709.

title: HDFC Bank trading slumps to 6-month low, select funds step up buying
